elements.before: Independent, lender-grade analysis for laundromat and self-service laundry acquisitions, buildouts, and refinancings across SBA 7(a) and 504, USDA Business & Industry, conventional bank, and equipment-finance capital. This page is our standing read on where laundromat demand and margin actually come from, how utility cost, turns-per-day, and lease risk sink feasibility forecasts, and the difference between the market study, the feasibility study, and the going-concern appraisal a lender requires.
elements.after: Buying or building a laundromat? Tell Feasibility Study Company about the store. The firm prepares feasibility studies of laundromats and self-service laundries for owners, buyers, developers and their lenders, starting each with a market study of the renters around the site. Renters are the core customer, and nearly 103 million people in the US rented as of 2023;20 the study maps that base in the trade area, then tests utility cost, turns per day, vend pricing and the lease term against debt service, for review by a 7(a) or 504 lender, a USDA B&I lender, a bank or an equipment finance company.
